title: Consumption Protection: per-plan safety bands, transparent invoice breakdowns, and automated credit remediations PRD
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Build a consumer‑facing and operator‑facing feature set that (1) places per-plan consumption safety bands to prevent catastrophic overrun events, (2) produces a line‑by‑line transparent invoice breakdown that maps tokens/embeddings/compute credits to cost drivers, and (3) automates first‑level credit remediation for transient incidents and predictable billing disputes. Goal is to reduce urgent billing support tickets by 40% and limit single‑customer overage spikes that breach SRE cost tolerances.
background: Problem: Customers with bursty workloads or misconfigured SDKs can unexpectedly exhaust soft quota windows, causing large overage invoices and support escalations. Internally, SREs absorb unpredictable spend and finance reconciliation is manual. Current instrumenting is per‑route usage metrics but lacking a customer‑bounded safety mechanism and clear invoice mapping. Related work: meter v2 (PM-41234) added per-route attribution; this PRD builds on that to tie entitlements, safety bands, and invoice remediation together.
goals: 1) User safety: auto‑apply configurable soft band actions (notifications, soft throttle, emergency credit buffer) before hard overage. 2) Transparency: invoices show itemized deltas (base plan allowance, burst credits used, compute‑surcharge, per‑model premium multipliers) with links back to call traces in console. 3) Operator ergonomics: automated crediting playbooks and one‑click dispute resolution for incidents with attached runbooks.
success_metrics: - 40% reduction in billing urgent support tickets within 90 days. - 90% of overage events mitigated by safety band actions (notify/soft throttle/preempt) before hard overage. - Median time to first‑contact credit remediation < 24h for qualifying incidents. - Invoices with drilldown adopted by 70% of active customers in pilot cohort.
scope: In scope: config model for per‑plan safety bands, console UI for safety band thresholds and incident rules, invoice line‑item expansion, hooks to automatic transient crediting, alerting and customer email templates, acceptance tests and analytics. Out of scope: changes to existing payment gateway settlement flows, new pricing tiers, and legal contract rewrite. Billing ledger remains canonical source of truth; we add reconciled annotations and dispute records.
requirements:
Functional requirements:
- R1: Per‑plan safety band configuration with 3 actions: Notify (email + console), Soft‑Throttle (graceful latency‑aware throttling), Apply‑Buffer (temporary emergency credits up to a configured cap).
- R2: Safety bands must be evaluated in the request path with O(1) latency impact; policy decisions can be served from cache with a 5s TTL.
- R3: Invoice must show: allowance used, burst credits consumed, emergency buffer applied, per‑token unit price (broken down by model variant), compute surcharge, tax lines, and dispute token. Each line must link to console trace or trace id.
- R4: Automated credit remediation: for incidents tagged as 'service outage' by SRE within 7 days, apply automated credit equal to documented lost tokens (formula below) and create dispute record.
- R5: Audit logging: all safety band events and automated credits must be logged to customer audit view and internal finance stream with immutable IDs.
- R6: Admin role required to modify safety bands; read access for billing viewers.
- R7: Opt‑in pilot flag for existing customers for 8 week pilot.
Non‑functional requirements:
- NFR1: Safety band evaluation adds <2ms p99 to request latency.
- NFR2: Invoicing render time for a customer with 30 days of history < 3s in console.
- NFR3: Compliance: any automated credit must generate an auditable justification (SRE incident id + summary) and a signed approval by billing automation key.
billing_acceptance_criteria:
- AC1: For a pilot customer, simulate a burst that crosses soft threshold; verify configured soft action triggers (notification + soft throttle) and no hard overage invoice charge appears for 48h when emergency buffer is applied.
- AC2: Generated invoice contains the following lines and matching links: base_allowance, consumption_over_allowance, emergency_buffer_credit, model_multipliers, compute_surcharge, taxes. Each line item must map to a consumption id.
- AC3: Automated credit flow applied by the system must appear in ledger with a dispute id and reduce billed amount on the invoice draft. Finance must be able to reconcile the credit within the ledger UI.
- AC4: All safety band changes require admin audit trail and who/when metadata. Attempts to change by non‑admin must be rejected.
- AC5: End‑to‑end test: purchase plan with 1000 token allowance, generate 1500 tokens in a burst; confirm the invoice shows 1000 base, 400 burst charged, 100 emergency buffer credited (if buffer configured to 100) and net billed amount consistent with unit prices.
- AC6: Performance: safety band evaluation and invoice rendering meet NFR latency budgets in test harness.
implementation_notes:
- Runtime/infra: Add a lightweight policy cache service associated with subscription records; store safety band rules in product catalog DB with versioning. Hook policy evaluation into the per‑request decision path with fast local cache and async backfill.
- Billing: extend invoice generator to accept annotated consumption records (consumption id -> model shard -> unit price). Create 'invoice annotations' table to persist derived lines for audit.
- Console: new 'Safety bands' settings page under Billing -> Plans; invoice drilldown page with trace links and dispute button.
- Automation: create an orchestration workflow (workflow id: billing_auto_credit_v1) that validates SRE incident tags and enacts credits via billing service API; requires a signed approval key.
- Data: add analytics events (safety_band.triggered, safety_band.action, emergency_credit.applied) and dashboards in metrics workspace.
- Rollout: feature-flag gated per‑customer; pilot with 5 customers (ops + AE selected).
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Tradeoff: Aggressive auto‑crediting reduces customer friction but increases finance workload and potential abuse. Decision: automated credits limited to incidents with SRE incident id and 7‑day window; credits capped per plan.
- Tradeoff: Tight evaluation path vs complexity of policy language. Decision: implement three primitive actions first (notify/soft_throttle/credit) and iterate on richer DSL in Q3.
- Feedback from sales: customers want clear invoice templates for enterprise finance approvals; we will provide exportable CSV + human friendly PDF.
- Legal review required to ensure automated credits do not create obligations beyond contract; flagged for legal signoff during pilot.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for policy cache behavior, TTL expiration and fallback.
- Integration tests that replay production‑like call traces and assert safety band triggers.
- End‑to‑end billing sandbox tests using synthetic customer and payment method: verify invoice lines and ledger updates.
- Load test: render invoices for 1000 customers concurrently to validate console rendering NFR.
- Customer acceptance test with pilot customers: scripted burst scenarios and manual invoice review.
deployment_plan:
- Phase 1: backend policy cache + billing annotations + API endpoints behind feature flag (internal). Deploy to staging and run end‑to‑end rehearsals.
- Phase 2: Console UI and pilot enablement for 5 customers. Monitor metrics and collect qualitative feedback.
- Phase 3: Gradual roll to 20% of customers with automation enabled; enable CSV/PDF export.
- Phase 4: GA once legal and finance signoffs complete and SRE runbook validated.
